title: The Forest of Tataka
captions: Beside the Sarayu river, Vishvamitra taught the princes two sacred mantras, Bala and Atibala. With them, they would never feel tired or hungry.
Next they crossed the great river Ganga by boat. From the dark forest ahead came a terrible roar that echoed over the water.
“This land was once green and happy,” said the sage. “Now the rakshasi Tataka lives here. She has the strength of a thousand elephants, and the people have fled.”
“Rama, end her terror and protect the people,” said Vishvamitra. Rama paused, for he had been taught never to harm a woman. “Protecting the helpless is a prince's dharma,” said the sage.
Rama remembered his father's words: obey the sage. He bowed and said, “I will do as you say, for the good of all.” Then he twanged his bowstring with a mighty sound.
Tataka rushed out, raising a storm of dust and hurling rocks. Rama's arrows turned the rocks aside, and with one true arrow the mighty rakshasi fell.
The forest grew calm and bright again. The gods rejoiced, and Vishvamitra blessed Rama with great joy. That night the princes rested peacefully in the forest.
value_meaning: doing what is right, protecting the helpless
lesson: Rama did not want to hurt anyone, and he thought carefully before he acted. But Tataka was frightening a whole land, and its people could not protect themselves. Our elders teach that dharma means doing what is right, and standing up for those who cannot protect themselves is right. Rama listened to his teacher and bravely did his duty for the good of all.
card_lesson: Rama thought carefully, listened to his teacher, and then bravely protected people who could not protect themselves. That is dharma: doing what is right.
question: Have you ever stood up for someone who needed help? Why was it the right thing to do?
